anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as manufacturing data (OEE, availability, performance rate, quality (first-pass yield), MTBF, good count, failures, assets). Ratios pool their parts (OEE and availability over planned production time, summed over shifts and machines before dividing), so a line's figure pools its machines' time; MTBF is run time per failure and assumes a constant failure rate; MTTR runs from actual start to actual finish of finished repairs, so repairs still open are not in it and it can read low. Readings are averaged, not time-weighted. Times are read in the zone they are written in (a file mixing offsets is read in UTC). The data covers 3 months, so month-over-month changes may be seasonal; there is no same month last year to compare with. Operators are people: figures by operator describe the work, never rank the people, and groups of fewer than 11 operators are not shown.

Is the Night shift gap in good count consistent across all lines, or is it concentrated on one or two lines?

report.executive_summary: Three months of sensor readings across 8 assets show 264 alarms, with vibration the clearest signal associated with alarm events. The dataset covers 17,630 cleaned readings from Aug–Oct 2026, capturing temperature, pressure, vibration, and alarm status across 8 assets and 3 production lines. Sensors S04, S05, and S06 stand out with notably higher average vibration than the other five sensors, which warrants closer attention.
technical_findings: Vibration (mm/s) and Alarm: r = 0.467 (n = 17,454; high confidence: 17454 rows)
mean Temperature by Line (3 groups) (n = 17,439; high confidence: 17439 rows)
mean Vibration (mm/s) by Sensor (8 groups) (n = 17,454; high confidence: 17454 rows)
Temperature: median 70.93, mean 71.01, range 66.04 to 77.18 (n = 17,439; high confidence: 17439 rows)
Vibration (mm/s): median 2.15, mean 2.43, range 0.093 to 16.18 (n = 17,454; high confidence: 17454 rows)
Alarm: median 0, mean 0.015, range 0 to 1.00 (n = 17,630; high confidence: 17630 rows)

recommended_actions.action: Investigate sensors S04, S05, and S06 for mechanical or mounting issues driving elevated vibration readings.
Review the export configuration to eliminate sentinel values (-9999 for temperature, 32767 for pressure) so missing readings are flagged at source rather than requiring post-hoc cleaning.
Investigate Line B's operating conditions to understand whether its higher average temperature relative to Line A is expected or a sign of a developing issue.
recommended_actions.reasoning: Temperature differences across lines may affect product quality or equipment wear.
recommended_actions.metric_impact: Temperature differences across lines may affect product quality or equipment wear.

anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as manufacturing data (assets, alarms). Ratios pool their parts (OEE and availability over planned production time, summed over shifts and machines before dividing), so a line's figure pools its machines' time; MTBF is run time per failure and assumes a constant failure rate; MTTR runs from actual start to actual finish of finished repairs, so repairs still open are not in it and it can read low. Readings are averaged, not time-weighted. Times are read in the zone they are written in (a file mixing offsets is read in UTC). The data covers 3 months, so month-over-month changes may be seasonal; there is no same month last year to compare with. A reading is a level: it is averaged over the period (each reading counts once; not time-weighted), never summed.

executive_view.headline: Three months of sensor readings across 8 assets show 264 alarms, with vibration the clearest signal associated with alarm events.

paragraphs.text: The dataset covers 17,630 cleaned readings from Aug–Oct 2026, capturing temperature, pressure, vibration, and alarm status across 8 assets and 3 production lines.
Sensors S04, S05, and S06 stand out with notably higher average vibration than the other five sensors, which warrants closer attention.

findings.text: Vibration (mm/s) and Alarm tend to move together.
Sensors S04, S05, and S06 average vibration of 3.15, 3.21, and 3.19 mm/s respectively, while the remaining five sensors all average between 1.97 and 2.01 mm/s.
Overall vibration ranges from 0.093 to 16.18 mm/s with a median of 2.15 mm/s, indicating that most readings are low but a tail of high readings exists.
Line B averages 71.99 °C and Line A averages 69.96 °C, with Line C at 71.14 °C, showing a modest spread in operating temperature across lines.
Average Temperature: Line B (71.99) is higher than Line A (69.96).

action_items.action: Investigate sensors S04, S05, and S06 for mechanical or mounting issues driving elevated vibration readings.
Review the export configuration to eliminate sentinel values (-9999 for temperature, 32767 for pressure) so missing readings are flagged at source rather than requiring post-hoc cleaning.
Investigate Line B's operating conditions to understand whether its higher average temperature relative to Line A is expected or a sign of a developing issue.
action_items.expected_impact: Temperature differences across lines may affect product quality or equipment wear.

findings.text: Sensor S07 averages 72.30 °C, while the remaining 11 sensors cluster tightly between 69.88 °C and 70.10 °C.
Vibration readings range from 0.102 to 10.73, and higher vibration moves together with failures, though the association is weak.
Temperature rose 3.5% month-over-month from Sep 2026 to Oct 2026; because only 3 months of data are available, it is not possible to tell whether this is seasonal.
Failures are rare events: the median reading shows no failure, and the mean across all 6,624 readings is 0.0234.
Average temperature: S07 (72.30) is higher than S12 (69.88).
